newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba hits back at U.S. over bomb case allegation.
newsitem.headline: Cuba hits back at U.S. over bomb case allegation.

text.p: Cuba on Thursday bitterly rejected U.S. accusations of "paranoia" over its charges that people responsible for bombing two Havana hotels last week came from the United States.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Miguel Alfonso criticised U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, accusing him of suffering from "verbal incontinence" and saying he appeared keen to please since he was ambitious to become an ambassador.
"His verbal incontinence seems to have been caught from the incontinence of Mrs. (Secretary of State Madeleine) Albright against us," Alfonso added.

Alfonso's remarks at a weekly news briefing were in repsonse to Burns' comments on Monday that he thought the Cuban government was paranoid for charging Americans were involved in the bombings without providing evidence.
Two small bombs went off in the lobbies of central Havana hotels the Nacional and the Capri on Saturday, slightly injuring three people and breaking windows.
The Cuban Interior Ministry said it had evidence that both the people responsible for the bombs and the material used came from the United States.
The statement did not say so, but it was clear official suspicion was falling on hardline critics of President Fidel Castro among the Cuban exile comunity in Florida.
The State Department has said it has asked the Cuban government to turn over any evidence Americans were involved in the bombings, but has not yet received any.
Alfonso said Cuba would present its proof when it felt the time and the occasion were right.
